transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Head of ML, Nereus), Tom Reeves (CTO, Nereus), Sanjay Rao (DevOps, Nereus), Maya Lin (Product, Nereus)

Summary:
Customer is evaluating a migration off OpenAI hosted endpoints to a Dedicated Redwood deployment (with potential Private/VPC later). Main concerns: eval parity (do responses match OpenAI outputs), compatibility with current vLLM/TGI tooling, latency & cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and ease of rollout. They want a benchmark run and security docs; next steps captured.

Topics:
- Current stack and why they want to migrate
- Technical compatibility: model weights, tokenization, vLLM/TGI interchangeability
- Performance: latency, throughput, batching, KV cache, quantization options
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
- Rollout plan: canary/gradual rollout, fallback to hosted, monitoring/eval parity

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine: Hi everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Jasmine from Redwood, AE on this account, with Marcus our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Alicia: Hey thanks, excited to talk through this. quick context - we run most inference on OpenAI right now, but costs are ramping and we need more control for compliance.
[00:20] Tom: yeah, and we also run some internal TGI/vLLM experiments for latency-sensitive routes. looking to understand if Redwood Dedicated buys us better economics without breaking evals.
[00:34] Marcus: great, that's exactly the kind of convo we do. curious - can you outline your current traffic profile and success criteria?
[00:42] Alicia: sure, mostly chat and some classification/rerank. about 2k qps peak at our busiest endpoints, average seq length ~120 tokens, and we care about p95 latency under 250ms for our chat route. quality-wise we need parity with OpenAI's GPT-4-ish outputs for a set of 150 eval prompts.
[01:05] Maya: also data residency; some customers require EU-only processing so region placement matters.
[01:12] Marcus: makes sense. for Dedicated we can pin region and isolate capacity. p95 under 250ms is achievable depending on model choice and batching strategy; there are tradeoffs with batching for throughput vs tail latency.
[01:30] Tom: can you run through the compatibility story - we use vLLM in prod for some models, and some teams prototype with TGI. will model files and tokenizers just work?
[01:42] Marcus: short answer: most of the commonly used open models are supported. longer: it's about the weights, tokenizer, and runtime options. Redwood's serving runtime accepts standard checkpoints, but there are nuances - tokenizer mismatches can cause subtle output diffs, and kv cache behavior differs slightly across runtimes which can affect generation on long-context prompts. we recommend a quick eval-parity run with your prompt set.
[02:10] Alicia: kv cache? you mean our prefix caching that vLLM handles?
[02:14] Marcus: yeah, KV cache - prefix caching and how the runtime reuses cached key/value tensors. Redwood does prefix/KV caching and continuous batching, but exact behavior can differ from vLLM; we'll surface differences in our benchmark.
[02:28] Sanjay: network question - for Dedicated we need VPC peering and our egress rules are locked down. can Redwood Dedicated sit inside our VPC or do we use a private link?
[02:39] Jasmine: we have both patterns. for Dedicated we offer a Private deployment option that integrates with your VPC, or dedicated capacity with secure peering. we'll send the network diagram and the set of IPs/ports.
[02:50] Tom: regulatory - SOC2? ISO? key management?
[02:53] Marcus: we're SOC2 Type II and have ISO certs, yes - we'll share our security pack. we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and audit logs + RBAC/SSO.
[03:07] Maya: good. on the eval parity piece - we've seen issues where outputs from open weights on other runtimes don't match exactly the OpenAI responses. how do you recommend we measure parity?
[03:18] Marcus: we suggest a 3-step approach: 1) run identical prompts against your OpenAI baseline and Redwood-hosted model variant to quantify token-level diffs and metric gaps, 2) tune sampling/temperature/penalty settings and retokenize to align tokenization, 3) if needed use small post-processing rules or fine-tune calibration. we'll help with step 1 and provide tooling for comparisons.
[03:42] Alicia: are there known gotchas with TGI/vLLM to Redwood? our infra team uses vLLM's batching queue specifics and some custom tokenizers.
[03:51] Marcus: the main gotchas are: different default context window handling, tokenizer special-case handling (e.g., BPE variants), attention kernel behaviors at long sequences, and quantization differences if you're using 4-bit. we can help map config parity; often it's a few config tweaks.
[04:08] Sanjay: about quantization - can Redwood Dedicated run 4-bit or 8-bit kernels efficiently? we currently run 4-bit with vLLM for cost reasons.
[04:17] Marcus: yes, our runtime supports quantized models and has optimized kernels for 8-bit and common 4-bit quant formats. performance and memory benefits depend on model architecture; we'll include recommended quant profiles per model during the benchmark.
[04:31] Tom: if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA and how do autoscaling and burst capacity work?
[04:37] Jasmine: Dedicated includes configurable autoscale policies - you can reserve baseline GPU capacity and allow burst to shared pools. we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated tiers; we'll share the SLA doc.
[04:50] Alicia: costs - can you ballpark per-token costs versus OpenAI? our CFO will want a delta.
[04:56] Jasmine: we can do scenario modeling. rough rule: for sustained high throughput, Dedicated per-token cost tends to be lower due to better GPU utilization and batching. but it depends on seq length, model, and utilization. we'll send a model showing hosted vs dedicated vs private TCO.
[05:14] Maya: what about function calling and streaming - we rely on streaming partial outputs to the client. do you support the same semantics?
[05:21] Marcus: yes, we support streaming responses and structured/function-style outputs. there can be minor framing differences but we support chunked streaming and deterministic function call outputs if you lock sampling.
[05:33] Alicia: for our evaluation, we need to test both classification/rerank and open-ended chat. can you do both in the benchmark?
[05:39] Marcus: absolutely. we'll set up a mixed workload test: chat (open gen), classification, and rerank. we'll measure accuracy metrics you supply and latency/cost.
[05:48] Tom: how much lift for our engineers to migrate? we have code that calls OpenAI SDK directly.
[05:54] Jasmine: Redwood's API is REST/SDK compatible and we provide a drop-in client shim for OpenAI-compatible calls. in many cases it's minimal code change: endpoint + key swap, and some config flags for streaming. for Dedicated/Private you also configure network and auth.
[06:10] Sanjay: about auth - do you support SAML SSO, RBAC per-team, and audit logs?
[06:16] Marcus: yes to all three. SAML/SSO for console, API keys for programmatic access, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. plus per-token usage breakdowns in the console.
[06:26] Alicia: curious about rollback/fallback - if we do a canary and see regressions, can we fall back to OpenAI with minimal pain?
[06:34] Marcus: yes we recommend a hybrid approach at first: route a fraction of traffic to Dedicated and keep automatic fallback to OpenAI on errors or mismatch. policy-based routing can be configured.
[06:45] Maya: do you have customers who've migrated from OpenAI to Dedicated and what were typical results?
[06:50] Jasmine: several - e.g., a fintech customer saw 35% per-token cost savings and improved p95 latency after tuning. we'll anonymize case studies and share them.
[06:59] Tom: for the benchmark run, what do you need from us?
[07:03] Marcus: ideally your eval prompt set, a sample of production requests (sanitized), success metrics and thresholds, and an account/endpoint for running tests. also whether you want hosted-first or try Dedicated pilot.
[07:16] Alicia: we'll provide the prompt set and a small sample. we prefer hosted-first benchmark to validate parity, then Dedicated pilot if results look good.
[07:25] Jasmine: that's a sensible path. we'll do hosted parity test, then Dedicated pilot configured to your VPC for smoke tests.
[07:33] Sanjay: network stuff again - what's the expected egress pattern during benchmarks? want to make sure our firewall rules cover it.
[07:39] Marcus: we'll provide IP ranges and endpoint URLs. for Dedicated inside VPC there's no public egress; forensic logs available.
[07:48] Maya: product question - can we pin models and do A/B rollouts for model variants?
[07:53] Marcus: yes, Redwood supports model pins, canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies.
[08:01] Alicia: is there a feature store or caching to speed up repeat prompts?
[08:06] Marcus: we support prefix caching/KV caching which helps repeat prefixes. we can also recommend a local LRU cache for deterministic inputs.
[08:16] Tom: about latency numbers - can you give us a sense: p95 for a 120 token reply on a typical 8xA100-like node?
[08:24] Marcus: rough ballpark: for an optimized compilation/kernels and with KV cache hits, p95 could be well under 250ms for medium-sized models. exact numbers depend on batching and quantization. we'll provide measured numbers in the benchmark.
[08:37] Alicia: what about model variants and checkpoints - are we locked to a Redwood curated catalog or can we bring our own?
[08:45] Marcus: you can bring your own weights; we also host a curated model catalog with verified performance profiles. BYO model requires some onboarding (tokenizer checks, potential conversion), which we help with.
[08:58] Sanjay: ops question - how are logs surfaced? do we push to our SIEM or do you retain logs for X days?
[09:06] Marcus: we stream audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM. retention is configurable; for Dedicated/Private we can match typical enterprise retention requests.
[09:18] Maya: approx timeline - we want a pilot in 4-6 weeks. realistic?
[09:23] Jasmine: yes. hosted parity test can run in ~1 week once we have prompts and samples; Dedicated pilot in your VPC usually 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals and procurement.
[09:33] Tom: procurement - any legal standard terms? do you support DPAs and data processing addenda?
[09:38] Jasmine: yes we have standard DPAs and enterprise contracts; we'll share legal and security docs.
[09:44] Alicia: will you run eval parity on both deterministic and sampling settings? some of our usage uses temperature 0 and some uses 0.7.
[09:52] Marcus: yes we'll mirror both modes. determinism is easier to compare; sampling comparisons use distribution metrics (e.g., BLEU-ish, embedding similarity) across a sample set.
[10:03] Sanjay: curious - you mentioned quantization differences earlier; if we bring 4-bit weights compiled by vLLM, do you recompile or do you require a different format?
[10:13] Marcus: we accept a couple standard quant formats; sometimes a conversion step is needed for best kernels. we'll detail supported formats and conversion steps in the onboarding pack.
[10:25] Maya: if Dedicated reduces cost, is there a minimum commit?
[10:29] Jasmine: Dedicated typically involves a capacity reservation with monthly/annual commit options. we'll share pricing tiers and flexibility options.
[10:37] Tom: security deep dive - after we sign off on pilot we'd like a 1-hour security session with your security lead.
[10:44] Jasmine: absolutely, we'll coordinate that.
[10:47] Alicia: okay let's talk specifics - for the hosted parity run, what exact artifacts do you need and what's the timeline?
[10:54] Marcus: need: 1) eval prompts (150 examples), 2) representative production sample (sanitized), 3) pass/fail criteria per prompt, 4) point of contact. once received we'll spin up the tests and share a report in ~5 business days.
[11:10] Maya: who runs the tests - is it your infra or do we run them in our environment?
[11:14] Marcus: we can run both. hosted parity tests run on Redwood-hosted instances; for Dedicated pilot we'll run benchmarks in your VPC or dedicated capacity.
[11:24] Tom: will you provide raw logs and diffs for inspection? we want to see example mismatches.
[11:29] Marcus: yes full diff reports and token-level traces for problematic prompts.
[11:34] Alicia: sounds good. one more - function call output formats sometimes differ; will that break our parsing?
[11:40] Marcus: usually not if you stick to structured JSON. we support the same function-calling primitives, but it's good to test with your parsers.
[11:49] Sanjay: are there limits on concurrency per key? we have spikes that hit short bursts.
[11:54] Marcus: Dedicated can be sized for bursts and we support autoscale policies and burst capacity. we'll size the pilot for your expected bursts.
[12:05] Jasmine: let's close with next steps and owners - Marcus will take the tech lead for benchmarks, Jasmine handles commercial and contract, Alicia will share evals.
[12:13] Marcus: I'll follow up with a checklist and schedule for the parity run.
[12:18] Alicia: thanks - we'll get the artifacts over this week.
[12:22] Tom: quick note - we sometimes use Azure-hosted endpoints; will Redwood integrate with Azure regions?
[12:28] Jasmine: yes we have multi-region options and cloud-region partners, including Azure in EU/US regions.
[12:36] Maya: any last open questions?
[12:38] Sanjay: none from infra.
[12:40] Alicia: no, good session.
[12:42] Jasmine: great, we'll send the security pack, pricing scenarios, and the benchmark checklist. thanks everyone.

[52:00] End of call.

Recap / Next steps:
- Jasmine to send pricing scenarios + SOW and legal/security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS notes).
- Marcus to schedule and run hosted parity benchmark once evals are received; prepare latency/cost estimates for Dedicated.
- Nereus to provide prompt set, sanitized sample traffic, and pass/fail thresholds.
- Schedule security deep-dive after pilot kickoff.
